title: Primary structure that stores the host system’s useful energy

concept.text: The innovation is a primary load-bearing structure that also stores and supplies the electrical energy needed for its host system’s useful mission. A vehicle chassis member or aircraft structural element would serve simultaneously as part of the load path and as an energy-storage device. Structural batteries provide the material basis for this idea by combining mechanical load bearing with electrochemical storage.

Scope synthesis: the defining advance would be demonstrated integration at the level of a working system. The structure must carry its declared loads and deliver useful mission energy while meeting requirements for aging, damage tolerance and safety. Installing conventional batteries inside a structural enclosure, or demonstrating energy storage and stiffness in a material specimen, would not by itself establish this capability. The supplied evidence establishes multifunctional material performance, but does not establish this mission-serving primary structure.

significance.text: Combining energy storage with primary structure could change how vehicles, aircraft and portable systems allocate mass. Material already needed to support loads could also contribute stored energy, reducing the requirement for separate batteries and making structural geometry, material selection and energy capacity parts of the same design problem. The 2024 paper identifies replacing structural vehicle parts while reducing conventional batteries as an intended application; this supports the integration opportunity, rather than proving complete mission-battery replacement.

System-level inference: a substantial net mass saving would be revolutionary for machines whose payload, range or endurance is constrained by mass, but its magnitude cannot be inferred from eliminating a separate pack alone. Usable energy, structural efficiency, electrical connections, protective systems, inspection access and repair provisions all enter the mass budget. A structural battery with lower energy per kilogram could still be advantageous if it replaces enough otherwise necessary structural mass; conversely, integration overhead could consume the benefit. A comparison against an equivalent conventional structure and battery system is therefore essential.

Application-boundary synthesis: ambient-energy harvesting is a separate capability because it generates energy from the environment, whereas this concept stores previously supplied energy. No numerical harvesting-power comparison is established here. Extending structural storage to occupied building frames or city-scale grid storage would require additional materials, fire-safety, durability and repair demonstrations. Results in carbon-fiber vehicle materials would not establish the suitability of ordinary building materials or the safety of embedding battery chemistry throughout occupied primary structure.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing capability in the supplied evidence is a primary member that supplies a declared useful mission’s energy and retains acceptable structural performance after electrochemical aging and relevant mechanical damage. The retained sources demonstrate the dual-function material concept and describe continuing investigation of mechanical and electrochemical interactions. They do not establish mission-scale qualification. This is an evidence boundary, not a finding that no later qualifying demonstration exists.

Engineering synthesis: the material must provide adequate usable energy and power while preserving stiffness, strength and load transfer. These functions must remain compatible during charging, discharging, repeated loading and environmental exposure. The central question is not simply whether both functions exist initially, but whether their interaction leaves sufficient margins over the intended service life. High initial longitudinal modulus and efficient charge transfer alone do not answer that question.

Engineering synthesis: scaling introduces joints, electrical connections, insulation, manufacturing variability, inspection and repair requirements. Impact or penetration can affect both the load path and the electrical system, so damage containment and residual structural capacity must be assessed together. Thermal events also require application-specific protection and a defined safe structural response. These are concrete qualification questions; the supplied retained evidence does not quantify their severity or establish their solutions.

The earlier research attributes a broader barrier list to the November 2025 review: low energy density, competing electrochemical and mechanical requirements, cost, fatigue and impact sensitivity, volume change, and a lack of standard tests. That publication has no retained text in the supplied evidence review. The list remains an attributed account requiring verification, rather than an inspected finding or proof that no applicable test methods exist.

current_state.text: Richa Chaudhary, Johanna Xu, Zhenyuan Xia and Leif E. Asp reported an all-carbon-fiber structural battery composite in “Unveiling the Multifunctional Carbon Fiber Structural Battery,” published online on 10 September 2024. The retained PubMed abstract reports energy density of 30 Wh/kg, cyclic stability up to 1000 cycles with approximately 100 percent coulombic efficiency, and elastic modulus above 76 GPa parallel to the fibers. These are reported material-level results. The retained evidence is an abstract, not the full research article, and does not establish specimen dimensions, mission-scale integration or structural certification.

Coulombic efficiency describes the relationship between charge delivered and charge supplied during cycling; it does not, by itself, establish retained energy capacity or mechanical durability. Likewise, the reported modulus is directional: performance parallel to the fibers cannot be treated as a complete description of structural behavior under other loading directions or damage conditions. The retained abstract does not provide the tensile-strength and post-cycling mechanical measurements asserted in the earlier account.

The earlier research attributes pristine tensile strength as high as about 790 MPa and post-cycling values of about 65 GPa modulus and 612 MPa strength in one configuration to Asp and Chaudhary’s “All-carbon fibre structural battery composites,” dated 23 February 2025. Its citation points to DOI 10.1177/1045389X251320443, but no source text was retained for the validated review. These numerical assertions remain unverified within this record and cannot establish a measured degradation trend without their test conditions, specimen correspondence and cycling history. Missing source text is not evidence that the values are false.

A retained Chalmers institutional article reports an ongoing study with energy density above 60 Wh/kg and elastic modulus above 100 GPa. The page was published on 24 June 2025 and updated on 27 January 2026, so its retained version cannot establish when each performance statement first appeared. These figures are verified as institutional statements about ongoing work; the underlying measurements and research paper were not inspected in the supplied review. They should not be presented as independently validated performance or a completed mission-scale demonstration.

Evidence-boundary synthesis: the supplied record contains no bounded freshness search establishing the field’s completeness through 1 November 2026. It therefore cannot determine whether a later mission-scale demonstration or a paper supporting the higher Chalmers figures had appeared by that date. The earlier comparison against contemporary lithium-ion packs exceeding 150 Wh/kg also lacks retained supporting evidence and is not used as a quantitative benchmark. These limitations leave the dated 2024 results intact.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: build a vehicle- or aircraft-scale primary element, or a complete small-vehicle chassis, that carries declared design loads and supplies the electrical energy required for a declared useful mission without a separate mission-energy pack. Specify mission duration, operating conditions, usable energy, required power, structural allowables and acceptance thresholds before testing. A material specimen reporting 30 Wh/kg and 76 GPa alone would not satisfy this proposed system-level criterion.
completion_criteria.label: Load-bearing primary structure powers a useful mission without separate packs

completion_criteria.text: Proposed durability and damage demonstration: repeat the structural and mission-energy assessments after a declared number of charge cycles and an application-relevant mechanical load history. Measure capacity retention and mechanical performance separately, and evaluate their interaction under representative operating conditions. Impact, penetration and fire tests should declare exposure conditions and required residual structural capacity, including the period over which that capacity must be maintained. These are proposed assessment criteria, not established consensus standards.
completion_criteria.label: Structural and energy performance assessed after cycling and mechanical loading

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical validation: report material composition, manufacturing methods, specimen geometry, interfaces, test procedures and variation across multiple builds. Independent reproduction should confirm both energy delivery and structural performance. A system comparison should include protection, connections, inspection and repair provisions, and should quantify any mass saving against an equivalent conventional structure and battery system.
completion_criteria.label: Independent reproduction confirms energy delivery and structural performance across builds

completion_criteria.text: Proposed boundary statement: define the demonstrated operating envelope, including temperature, loading directions, service duration, allowable damage and repair assumptions. Finite testing can establish performance across that declared envelope; it cannot establish universal durability or safety under every mission and damage scenario. Qualification would remain specific to the intended application and its applicable requirements.
completion_criteria.label: Declare the demonstrated operating envelope and application-specific qualification limits

related_concepts.text: Roster-based synthesis: STR-01, “Flaw-tolerant bulk members at near-theoretical specific strength,” concerns structural performance despite flaws. It overlaps STR-08 where damage tolerance affects safe energy-bearing members, but exceptional specific strength does not establish useful energy storage. STR-02, “Repeated autonomous restoration of full structural capacity,” addresses recovery after damage. Combining it with STR-08 would additionally require restoration or safe isolation of damaged electrochemical functions; neither capability implies the other.

Roster-based synthesis: STR-03, “A cast mineral solid that can be a complete primary structure,” shares the goal of extending a material’s structural role, but concerns a different material system and does not imply electrochemical storage. STR-05, “Primary members whose mechanical state can be reprogrammed in service,” and STR-06, “Load-bearing structures that grow and remodel,” concern changes to mechanical behavior or structural form. STR-08 could potentially supply energy for such functions, but storage alone establishes neither reprogramming nor growth.

Roster-based synthesis: STR-04, “Field-scale broadband seismic cloaking,” STR-10, “Ordinary buildings that remain undamaged and usable after design-level earthquakes,” and STR-11, “Passive damping that removes resonant amplification from governing modes,” address structural response to excitation or earthquake damage. Their overlap with STR-08 is the need to preserve load-bearing performance under relevant dynamic conditions. Energy storage does not itself provide seismic cloaking, prevent earthquake damage or establish passive damping.

Roster-based synthesis: STR-07, “Topological control that denies an undesigned collapse mechanism,” and STR-12, “Disproportionate collapse made unavailable after loss of any one primary member,” address system-level collapse behavior. They become relevant when damage to an energy-storing primary member could compromise the load path. STR-08 would need an appropriate structural safety strategy, but multifunctional material performance does not establish either collapse-control capability.

Roster-based synthesis: STR-09, “A prospectively validated law of structural lifespan,” overlaps directly with the need to understand coupled electrochemical aging and structural service life. STR-08 requires credible durability evidence for its declared application; it does not require, or establish, a general predictive law of structural lifespan. The concepts remain distinct even if lifespan prediction would make structural batteries easier to design and maintain.

unresolved_issues: The supplied evidence does not establish whether a qualifying mission-serving primary structure had been demonstrated by 1 November 2026.

The underlying study, measurement conditions and publication status supporting Chalmers’ figures above 60 Wh/kg and 100 GPa remain unverified; the date those statements first appeared is also unresolved.

The Sage article’s reported strength and post-cycling values require source verification, including specimen correspondence, loading direction and cycling conditions. The review’s recommendation to remove these numbers entirely was not adopted because the user explicitly requested preservation of unresolved quantitative detail; they are retained only as unverified attributions.
The November 2025 review’s exact barrier discussion and authorship remain unverified because no text was retained.
Capacity retention, post-aging structural allowables, combined damage-and-cycling behavior, specimen dimensions and certification status cannot be established from the retained 2024 abstract.
No supported system-level comparison establishes net mass savings or a contemporary conventional-pack energy-density benchmark.
The proposed completion criteria still require application-specific numerical thresholds and qualification requirements before they can become an executable demonstration program.

brief.title: Vehicle frames that also store their power
possible: A vehicle could run on energy stored in the frame that holds it together. An aircraft could draw power from its own supporting structure. Those parts would carry the required loads and supply enough electricity for a useful journey without a separate battery pack.
why: Vehicles, aircraft and portable machines could devote less weight to separate batteries. Materials already needed for support would also store energy, potentially leaving more weight available for carrying people or cargo, travelling farther or running longer.

sources.who: Richa Chaudhary, Johanna Xu, Zhenyuan Xia and Leif E. Asp
sources.showed: They built a carbon-fiber material that stores electricity and carries loads. They measured stiffness along the fibers and reported repeated charging and discharging.
sources.quote: Here, an all-carbon fiber-based structural battery is demonstrated utilizing the pristine carbon fiber as negative electrode, lithium iron phosphate (LFP)-coated carbon fiber as positive electrode, and a thin cellulose separator.
sources.cited_for: The same material can provide mechanical support and store electrical energy.
sources.not_established: The material tests do not establish a working vehicle structure that supplies journey energy and remains safe after aging and damage.

sources.who: Leif E. Asp and Richa Chaudhary
sources.showed: This is a study of carbon-fiber materials that combine battery storage with structural support, including strength measurements after repeated charging.
sources.cited_for: It addresses strength and stiffness before and after repeated charging.
sources.not_established: Those measurements alone would not establish durability in a working vehicle under combined electrical use and mechanical damage.

sources.showed: This is a review of the design, manufacture and challenges of materials that combine structural support with battery storage.
sources.cited_for: It discusses obstacles to combining energy storage with mechanical support.
sources.not_established: A review of challenges does not demonstrate a structure that powers a useful journey.

sources.showed: Chalmers reports doubled combined storage and structural performance in an ongoing study. Researchers are also investigating how mechanical stress and battery use affect each other.
sources.quote: In an ongoing study, researchers have shown that the multifunctional performance can be doubled.
sources.cited_for: Chalmers reports further material improvements and continuing work on interactions between loading and energy use.
sources.not_established: The ongoing study does not establish independently reproduced performance or a structure that powers a complete useful journey.

shown: Chaudhary and colleagues built a carbon-fiber material that both supports loads and stores electricity. It stored 30 watt-hours per kilogram, a measure of energy relative to weight. Its stiffness was measured along the fibers.

Chalmers reports further improvements in an ongoing study. The demonstrated advance remains at the material level; a supporting structure that powers a useful journey still needs a system demonstration.
missing: A main supporting structure must carry its declared loads and supply a useful journey’s energy without a separate battery pack.
Energy storage and structural performance must remain adequate together after repeated charging, loading and relevant damage.
Connections, protection, inspection and repairs must work at full scale, with a safe structural response to battery fires.
Independent builds and a complete comparison must establish whether the combined structure actually saves weight.

milestones.label: A supporting structure powers a useful journey
milestones.explanation: A vehicle-scale supporting part or small-vehicle chassis would have to carry specified loads and power a declared journey without a separate battery pack. This would establish useful operation beyond material samples.

milestones.label: Support and energy delivery survive use and damage
milestones.explanation: Tests would have to measure energy storage and structural performance after repeated charging, loading and specified damage or fire exposure. This would establish whether both functions retain adequate margins.

milestones.label: Independent builds confirm performance and measure weight savings
milestones.explanation: Independent builds would have to reproduce energy delivery and structural performance, with a complete weight comparison against separate structures and batteries. This would establish repeatability and any practical weight benefit.

milestones.label: Operating conditions and qualification limits are defined
milestones.explanation: Testing would have to define supported temperatures, loading directions, service life, damage and repair assumptions. This would establish which uses the demonstrated performance and safety actually cover.

uncertain: How much weight would the complete system save once protection, connections, inspection access and repairs are included?
How do battery aging and mechanical damage affect each other over the intended service life?
What performance thresholds and damage exposures would qualify the structure for each intended use?

page.title: Primary structures made from structural battery composites
page.definition: A structural battery composite—a material that stores electrical energy while carrying mechanical loads—forms part of a host system’s primary load path and supplies its specified mission-energy demand. The integrated structure meets the host’s structural and electrical qualification requirements.

goal.need: MATISSE cites a Boeing 787 auxiliary battery weighing 28 kg per pack, with 102 Wh/kg at cell level and 79 Wh/kg at pack level. It defines structural-battery performance per kilogram added to an equivalent unpowered component, making displaced structural mass part of the energy-storage mass budget.

statements.quote: Develop structural materials with integrated capabilities such as batteries, supercapacitors, and photovoltaics.
statements.context: The objective appears under “Structures with Integrated Energy Generation and Energy Storage” in NASA’s Nanotechnology Area Roadmap.

statements.quote: achieving an aircraft structural element capable of functioning as a battery module.
statements.context: The programme proposes integrating lithium-ion cells into aircraft composites so that the cells share the load-bearing function.

completion.title: A qualified primary structural battery supplies its host’s energy demand throughout a specified mission.
completion.criterion: A host completes its specified mission using energy stored in a structural battery composite that participates in its primary load path. The final integrated configuration must previously have met the host’s applicable structural, electrical, environmental, ageing and damage-tolerance qualification requirements. Energy, power, loads and service life are specified for that application; no universal specific-energy, cycle-life or mission-duration minimum is imposed.
completion.set_by: Atlas synthesis, adapting NASA’s qualification and mission-operation stages; no structural-battery-specific completion standard was located.
completion.basis: Searched NASA’s structural-materials roadmap, MATISSE/SOLIFLY requirements and airworthiness work, Navy SBIR N232-086, and ASTM/IEC structural-battery qualification searches. These provide maturity criteria and application-specific targets, but no test specifically establishing primary structure supplying a host’s complete mission-energy demand. Qualification followed by actual mission operation adapts NASA TRL 8–9.

milestones.title: A structural battery demonstrates load bearing and energy storage in laboratory tests.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate both functions through bench or coupon tests, with material properties and models covering the intended functions, as required by Navy SBIR Phase I. Chaudhary and colleagues reported 30 Wh/kg at 0.025C and 76 GPa longitudinal modulus on 10 September 2024. Mechanical coupons were approximately 30 × 3 mm. After 1,000 electrochemical cycles, the cellulose-separator cells had approximately 65 GPa modulus; reported maximum average stress fell from 790 to 612 MPa, with 3–5 specimens per cell type. These are material results, not qualification allowables.
milestones.set_by: US Department of the Navy, SBIR topic N232-086, Phase I; the solicitation covers multifunctional aircraft materials, including structural batteries.
milestones.threshold_quote: Demonstrate the proposed concept through laboratory bench testing and/or coupon testing, as appropriate.

milestones.title: A structural battery wingtip stores 140 Wh and withstands 1.15 times its limit loads.
milestones.criterion: MATISSE specifies 140 Wh capacity and testing at 1.15 times limit loads, at room temperature in dry conditions. Acceptance requires no visible cracks or permanent deformation, functioning batteries within operating limits, and displacements similar to predictions. Test one battery wingtip against one reference wingtip. On 13 July 2026 the consortium announced a tested 40-cell wingtip, without publishing every acceptance result there; this announcement is not peer reviewed.
milestones.set_by: MATISSE consortium, D1.1, sections 5.2 and 6; this research protocol is specific to its aircraft wingtip demonstrator.
milestones.threshold_quote: Electrical performance degraded but still functional.

milestones.title: A structural-battery subsystem prototype operates under its critical environmental conditions.
milestones.criterion: A high-fidelity subsystem prototype addresses critical scaling issues and operates in a relevant environment under critical environmental conditions, with performance agreeing with analytical predictions. This applies NASA’s general TRL 6 hardware criterion.
milestones.set_by: NASA Earth Science Technology Office, TRL 6 hardware description and exit criteria; the criterion appears only in the published TRL table.

milestones.title: A structural-battery prototype operates on its host platform in the operational environment.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate a high-fidelity engineering unit on its actual operational platform, addressing critical scaling issues and matching predicted performance: NASA’s general TRL 7 criterion. Thomas and Qidwai reported in March 2005 that a 171 g Wasp aircraft prototype flew for 1 hour 47 minutes on one charge using four wing structure-battery cells weighing 98 g. That reinforced polymer-cell architecture is distinct from the all-carbon-fibre composite; the paper assigns no TRL rating.
milestones.set_by: NASA Earth Science Technology Office, TRL 7 hardware description and exit criteria; the criterion appears only in the published TRL table.

milestones.title: The final structural-battery system passes qualification for its intended platform and environment.
milestones.criterion: Successfully demonstrate the final product in its final configuration through testing and analysis for its intended operational environment and platform, with test performance verifying analytical predictions. This is NASA’s general TRL 8 hardware criterion.
milestones.set_by: NASA Earth Science Technology Office, TRL 8 hardware description and exit criteria; the criterion appears only in the published TRL table.

not_found: No located source documented final-configuration qualification followed by mission operation for primary structure made from a structural battery composite.
No public result establishing passage of every MATISSE full-scale acceptance criterion was located.
The SOLIFLY roadmap and airworthiness deliverable links returned download wrappers without readable documents.
The supplied Electrochimica Acta review and the newer High-energy cathode in carbon fibre structural battery paper could not be opened.

results.detail: The abstract also reports energy storage at 30 Wh/kg. It does not report models covering the intended functions, as required by the criterion.
results.quote: Remarkably, the elastic modulus of the all-fiber structural battery exceeds 76 GPa when tested in parallel to the fiber direction - by far highest till date reported in the literature.

results.finding: Structural battery composites, sample size not stated, achieved over 60 Wh/kg.
results.detail: The source also reports an elastic modulus over 100 GPa, but does not describe the tests or models for the ongoing study.
results.quote: The structural battery composites exhibit an energy density of over 60 Wh/kg and an elastic modulus of over 100 GPa.

results.finding: Moderately stitched structural battery, sample count not stated: 42.2 Wh/kg at 0.1C.
results.detail: The study also reports flexural strength of 215.6 MPa, modulus of 14.7 GPa, and energy performance under bending. An equivalent-circuit model is described for electrochemical impedance, but the excerpt does not report a mechanical model covering the load-bearing function.

results.detail: The company reports operation in volcanic dust and thermal swings, but does not establish critical environmental limits, resolution of scaling issues, or agreement with analytical predictions.
results.quote: On board, integrated into the rover frame, our Volta Structural Battery: 1 kWh of energy in a load-bearing panel 34 mm thick, carrying shear loads as part of the structure while powering onboard payloads during the campaign.

results.finding: One heavy-lift drone was flight-tested with a 7.5 kWh structural battery pack.
results.detail: The source describes the battery as the drone’s structural spine and reports a battery-only flight test.
